name: Selway River
agency: USFS Bitterroot National Forest, West Fork Ranger District

camps.name: Bad Luck Bar
camps.desc: A large high-water camp. Bad Luck Creek enters on the right 0.3 mile downstream.

camps.name: Waldo Bar
camps.desc: A large high-water camp with few trees.

camps.name: Driftwood Bar
camps.desc: A medium camp at moderate flow.

camps.name: Running Creek bridge camp
camps.desc: A camp before the trail bridge to a private ranch on the left. Often has horseflies.

camps.name: Running Creek Flat
camps.desc: A large wooded high-water camp with no sandy beach; a swimming hole by the trail.

camps.name: Archer
camps.desc: A large high-water camp with a sandy beach. North Star ranch (private) is across the river.

camps.name: Goat Creek
camps.desc: A small high-water camp and lunch stop.

camps.name: Pom Beach
camps.desc: A small low-water camp.

camps.name: Little Goat Creek
camps.desc: An excellent large camp at moderate flow, in a rapid, with a swimming hole below.

camps.name: Cougar Flats
camps.desc: Near Ditch Creek and the private Selway Lodge.

camps.name: White Trail Flats
camps.desc: A large high-water camp.

camps.name: Mills Camp
camps.desc: A large high-water camp, 0.2 mile below White Trail Flats.

camps.name: Bear Creek
camps.desc: A small low-water camp at the creek mouth.

camps.name: Big Cedar (island camp)
camps.desc: A large high-water camp on the left; a medium low-water camp on the right. An island splits the river.

camps.name: Black Sands
camps.desc: A large camp at moderate flow, with a cave and a swimming hole nearby.

camps.name: Dead Elk
camps.desc: A medium low-water camp with a sandy beach and a swimming hole.

camps.name: Rattlesnake Bar
camps.desc: A medium high-water camp with no swimming hole.

camps.name: Roots
camps.desc: A small camp at moderate flow.

camps.name: Tony Point bridge camp
camps.desc: A medium high-water camp above the suspension bridge; an emergency camp on the left below. A trail leads about a mile to the Moose Creek ranger station.

camps.name: Tony Point
camps.desc: An excellent medium high-water camp with a sandy beach and a shallow swimming hole.

camps.name: Divide Creek
camps.desc: A medium camp at moderate flow.

camps.name: Meeker Creek
camps.desc: A good camp at moderate flow at the creek mouth.

camps.name: Tango Bar
camps.desc: An excellent large camp at moderate flow with a big sandy beach and a swimming hole.

camps.name: Trapper Camp (Marten Creek)
camps.desc: Marten Creek enters on the left; this camp is about 0.2 mile upstream.

camps.name: Boulder Bar
camps.desc: 0.3 mile above Dry Bar.

camps.name: Dry Bar
camps.desc: A beautiful medium camp at moderate flow.

camps.name: Upper Pinchot
camps.desc: A medium camp at moderate flow.

camps.name: Lower Pinchot
camps.desc: A large high-water camp.

camps.name: Ballinger
camps.desc: A medium high-water camp at the creek mouth.

camps.name: Tee Kem
camps.desc: An excellent medium camp at moderate flow just below the falls, with a swimming hole.

camps.name: Cupboard
camps.desc: A medium camp at moderate flow near Cupboard Creek.

camps.name: Renshaw
camps.desc: A good camp below Renshaw Rapid with a sandy beach and a swimming hole.

rapids.name: Rocky rapids below launch
rapids.desc: Tight for rafts.

rapids.name: Slalom Slide
rapids.desc: A boulder bar with a diagonal channel.

rapids.name: Galloping Gertie
rapids.desc: Hard at low water; rafts can wedge on the left. Enter right.

rapids.name: Washer Woman
rapids.desc: Scout from the center or right. Especially hard for rafts at low flow, with a good chance of sticking: pick where to stick. American Whitewater rates it IV.

rapids.name: Cougar Bluff
rapids.desc: A wave train along the left cliff.

rapids.name: Holy Smokes
rapids.desc: Possibly II+ at low water.

rapids.name: Ping Pong Alley
rapids.desc: Rated II on the Forest Service map but hard for rafts at low flow, with a lot of pushing off rocks.

rapids.name: Goat Creek Rapid
rapids.desc: Large boulders; a boulder garden. Watch for logs early in the season.

rapids.name: Selway Lodge Bridge Rapid
rapids.desc: Rafts often stick on exposed rocks at low flow.

rapids.name: Bear Creek Rapid
rapids.desc: About 0.2 mile below Bear Creek camp.

rapids.name: Rodeo Rapid
rapids.desc: Likely just below Black Sands.

rapids.name: Pettibone Rapid
rapids.desc: Follows Dead Elk camp.

rapids.name: False Ham
rapids.desc: Just above Ham.

rapids.name: Ham Rapid
rapids.desc: Two major drops through big boulders and a narrow channel; precise moves are required. Named for a dinner ham lost there in 1961.

rapids.name: Hell Creek rapids
rapids.desc: The start of nearly continuous Class II+ rapids.

rapids.name: Tony Point Rapid
rapids.desc: Plan your route at low water.

rapids.name: Double Drop
rapids.desc: Two drops after Jake Creek. At higher flows they merge into one big rapid; good recovery at low flow.

rapids.name: Wa-Poots (Grizzly Saddle)
rapids.desc: A steep bedrock chute at low flow; an S-turn with rocks on the outside corners.

rapids.name: The Ladle
rapids.desc: The hardest rapid on the run at any flow. A complex boulder garden; scout from the trail on river right. A sneak route on the far left works for kayaks and canoes.

rapids.name: Little Niagara
rapids.desc: Big hydraulics at higher flows; usually run down the right side, close to the cliff.

rapids.name: Puzzle Creek
rapids.desc: A waterfall over a meter high, right of center.

rapids.name: Miranda Jane
rapids.desc: A Class II rapid comes first.

rapids.name: Meeker Rapid
rapids.desc: Per the Forest Service map;

rapids.name: Osprey
rapids.desc: A steep drop among boulders.

rapids.name: Three Links Rapid
rapids.desc: Per the Forest Service map; about 0.4 mile below the pack bridge.

rapids.name: Wolf Creek Rapid
rapids.desc: Scout from the trail or island. Rafts usually run the right tongue and ferry right; watch for laterals at higher flows and a ledge hole at the bottom at low flow.

rapids.name: Tee Kem Falls (Jims Creek Falls)
rapids.desc: Jims Creek's debris fan pushes the river to the right bank; follow the tongue right. Rated IV by American Whitewater.

rapids.name: Cupboard Rapid
rapids.desc: Per the Forest Service map; may be easier at low flow.

rapids.name: Renshaw Rapid
rapids.desc: A stiff drop along the left bank into a cliff.

rapids.name: Selway Falls
rapids.desc: Not runnable. Selway Falls is a Class VI hazard just below the take-out, with massive boulders, surging boils and sieves. Take out at Race Creek and view it from the overlook on the road.

hikes.name: White Cap Creek guard station
hikes.desc: About half a mile up White Cap Creek from the launch, with a nice campsite.

hikes.name: Running Creek swimming hole
hikes.desc: Around the corner below the creek mouth.

hikes.name: Shearer guard station
hikes.desc: A Forest Service station with a public airstrip upstream.

hikes.name: Black Sands cave
hikes.desc: A cave and swimming hole near camp.

hikes.name: Moose Creek ranger station
hikes.desc: About a mile on trail from the suspension bridge at Tony Point.

indigenous: The Selway country is part of the homeland of the Nez Perce (Nimiipuu), whose travel routes crossed the Bitterroot Mountains. Respect any cultural sites you find and leave them undisturbed.
history: A wilderness river from the start

The Selway–Bitterroot Wilderness was among the first areas protected by the Wilderness Act of 1964, and the entire Selway was included in the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act of 1968. That early protection is why the corridor is so undeveloped and why use is limited to one launch per day in season.

Forest Service guard stations such as Shearer and Moose Creek, and pack bridges like the one at Three Links, are reminders of the days when rangers lived in the backcountry and supplies came in by mule and by airstrip.
geology: The Selway runs through the Bitterroot Mountains, whose core is granite and gneiss of the Idaho Batholith. The hard rock helps explain the narrow canyon and the boulder-choked, technical rapids.
lore: The river is crucial habitat for bull trout and Chinook salmon, and it holds one of the last strains of wild steelhead in the lower 48 not influenced by hatcheries.

rules.d: The Four Rivers permit covers private, non-commercial floats. Outfitted trips follow separate authorizations.
The Selway runs through the Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness. Leave No Trace applies, with no motorized equipment and no mechanized travel.
The Paradise gauge is the one that matters at the ramp. Rafts need about 0.9 ft to launch, kayaks 0.5 ft and inflatable kayaks 0.1 ft; above about 5 ft the river is dangerous.
Camp at moderate-flow sites in normal water; at high flow use the ones marked high-water. After Moose Creek about 7 miles have no large camps, so plan your night before scouting the Ladle.
Pack out solid waste in a washable, reusable toilet system. Giardia is a risk; filter or treat all drinking water.
Fire restrictions change through the season. Use a fire pan and burn only small dead wood. Check with the West Fork Ranger Station.
Store food and trash away from the boats and camp. Selway corridor is active bear country.
Scout the Ladle from the trail on river right. Wolf Creek is also scouted, from the trail or island.
Do not float past the take-out. Selway Falls, less than half a mile below, is Class VI.
Late June is usually the most dependable. Peak melt in early June can be dangerous, and flows are often too low by mid-July. Flows can rise sharply overnight.

landmarks.name: Paradise launch
landmarks.desc: Wooden boat ramp at 3,050 ft below the White Cap Creek confluence. Campground with 11 sites, vault toilets and a host who checks permits.

landmarks.name: Running Creek bridge
landmarks.desc: A trail bridge to a private ranch; the first place below the launch to cross on foot.

landmarks.name: Shearer
landmarks.desc: Forest Service guard station and airstrip.

landmarks.name: Selway Lodge
landmarks.desc: Private lodge reached by a pack bridge; the river crossing at Ditch Creek.

landmarks.name: Hell Creek
landmarks.desc: The start of continuous Class II+ rapids.

landmarks.name: Tony Point suspension bridge
landmarks.desc: A trail to the Moose Creek ranger station.

landmarks.name: Moose Creek confluence
landmarks.desc: The largest tributary; nearly doubles the flow and picks up the gradient to about 50 feet per mile. About 7 miles with no large camps follow.

landmarks.name: Pack bridge
landmarks.desc: Three Links Creek enters right, Mink Creek left.

landmarks.name: Race Creek campground
landmarks.desc: On the right bank, reached by road.

landmarks.name: Race Creek take-out
landmarks.desc: A boat ramp below the campground and above the bridge to Selway Falls. Selway Falls is just downstream.

notes.camp: *Choose camps by water level: sites marked high-water stay dry when the river is up and moderate-flow sites need lower water. Bears and cougars are active in the corridor, so store food and trash away from camp and boats.
notes.hike: *Trails are mostly short walks to guard stations and swimming holes. Check for ticks and poison ivy, and carry out everything you pack in; the corridor is wilderness.

permit.status: Required May 15 to July 31 · one party per day · lottery

items.d: Apply online on Recreation.gov from December 1 to January 31. Hard copy applications are not accepted. The Selway is part of the Four Rivers lottery, with one application per lottery and one permit and launch reservation during the season.
Results are emailed on February 14 and are viewable in your Recreation.gov profile.
Accept your reservation by March 15. After confirming you receive regulations you must read in full.
Cancelled or unconfirmed dates are released March 16 at 8:00 a.m. Mountain, first come, first served. Late-season dates in mid to late July are easiest to get, but flows are often too low.
Pick up the permit at the West Fork Ranger Station in Darby, Montana, up to 14 days before launch.
$6 non-refundable application fee. No per-person recreation fee.

The control season is May 15 to July 31. Pre-season trips must be off the river by 11:59 p.m. May 14; post-season trips cannot launch before August 1. No permit is required outside the control season.
One party of up to 16 people may launch each day in the control season. Outside it, groups are limited to 20 and there is no daily limit.

The permit holder must be 18 by the launch date and is the responsible person. Private non-commercial floats only. Launch date and holder cannot be changed after issuance; group size, exit date and watercraft can be changed before issuance.
Cancel on Recreation.gov at least 15 days before launch.
A late cancellation or no-show bars you from holding a Selway permit for one year.
The 15-day rule is waived if the river is above 5 feet at the Paradise gauge or snow blocks the road to Paradise, but you must still cancel.
